What we have is an underlying determination to posit a contrast between concepts and empirical data. If you will indulge me, I'll separate AI and humans from the discussion for a bit, and talk about that.

Whereas humans up to now have always tried to form the idea of the good, for example, and to establish it as a norm to guide our thinking and action, when it comes to transformers, the emphasis is on the regularities that are observed in a probabilistic environment. From the perspective of a philosophical science [Wissenschaft] – and no AI seems to aspire to that – the dominance of ‘data’ as opposed to concepts means that we are presented with something that is directly given, not able to be shown in conditions of abstract contestation, and which we can observe only as a fait accompli.

This movement from idea to data is given expression in the space between the late Kant and late Wittgenstein. Whereas Kant sought virtue, duty, and a normative-teleological outlook to configure a common world, Wittgenstein's sceptical-analytical reformulations can only then speak of use, rule following, and obedience. The manner of prescription and description ('how we use words', 'how we form sentences') flips despite the apparent continuation of philosophical enthrallment to a logocentric discourse with the world. To use Ortega Y Gasset's rationale, Wittgenstein switched from seeking origination values, or statuses established a priori, to statuses established a posteriori.

The emphasis on statistics, again, comes back to the fact that we no longer consider it possible to establish one true moral, political, or logical norm over and above the individual instances that in some probablistic sense condition human conduct in the first place. If you like, we no longer practice Socratic philosophy because we want to recalibrate dogmatism in observed tendencies. This is what data and statistics are all about.

For the above reason, I am minded of Peter Strawson's felicity, whereby phenomena interdigitate in a posteriori determinations supported by concepts (in their turn cogensorially earned as regard validation) to seek out 'fitness for purpose'.
